featured.title: The US Just Blocked Foreigners From Anthropic's Best AI. Indian Engineers Are in the Crossfire.
featured.excerpt: Commerce Secretary Lutnick's export ban on Fable 5 and Mythos 5 hits Anthropic's foreign-born workforce, TCS's new Claude deployment, and every Indian company that was using these models to patch vulnerabilities.
featured.image_caption: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei at TechCrunch Disrupt
featured.nri_angle: Indian engineers at Anthropic are barred from using the models they helped build, TCS's 50,000-employee Claude deployment faces regulatory uncertainty, and Indian enterprise customers lose access to critical cybersecurity tools.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

editorial.title: From Memes to Monarchy: RCB's Dynasty Has Arrived
editorial.excerpt: Royal Challengers Bengaluru retain the IPL title with a five-wicket demolition of Gujarat Titans in Ahmedabad — and a 15-year-old from Sambalpur might just have stolen the entire season.
editorial.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America's Top Trade Negotiator Will Fly to India the Week After G7. A Deal, Officials Say, Is Possible.
news.excerpt: USTR Jamieson Greer's visit follows months of back-and-forth on tariffs, Section 301 probes, and a bilateral framework that could reshape how NRIs send goods — and money — across both countries.
news.image_caption: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer at his official portrait session
news.nri_angle: A US-India trade deal directly affects NRI remittances, tariffs on Indian exports, H-1B visa policy, and the cost of goods flowing between the two countries.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Tata's iPhone Parts Factory Faces Shutdown Threat After Regulators Find Contaminated Farmland Water.
news.excerpt: Tamil Nadu's pollution board says wastewater from Tata Electronics' Hosur plant overflowed into nearby agricultural wells. Tata says its own tests show full compliance.
news.image_caption: Electronic circuit boards in a production facility
news.nri_angle: India's rise as a global iPhone manufacturing hub is a point of pride for the diaspora — but recurring supply chain problems raise questions about whether growth is outpacing environmental governance.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Has Built Twenty Foundational AI Models. Five Are Already Live. The World Barely Noticed.
news.excerpt: The IndiaAI Mission is funding sovereign language models, video generators, and medical diagnostics AI — all designed to work in 22 Indian languages. The goal is not to beat OpenAI but to make sure India never depends on it.
news.image_caption: Server racks inside a modern data center powering AI workloads
news.nri_angle: NRI tech professionals and investors increasingly have a stake in India's AI ecosystem — from Sarvam AI's enterprise models to the GPU infrastructure boom attracting billions in private capital.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Modi Lands in Nice and Heads to Bratislava. No Indian PM Has Ever Visited Slovakia.
news.excerpt: The six-day European tour includes the first-ever prime ministerial visit to the Slovak Republic, a bilateral with Macron, and a G7 seat at Evian where he may face Trump for the first time since the tariff war.
news.image_caption: Bratislava Castle, where Slovak PM Robert Fico will welcome Modi on June 15
news.nri_angle: Modi is expected to discuss H-1B visas, trade tariffs, and energy cooperation with Trump at the G7 — all issues that directly shape life for millions of NRIs in the US and Europe.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Infrastructure Budget Has Nearly Doubled in Five Years. It Is Now the Largest Public Works Push in the Country's History.
news.excerpt: Rs 12.2 trillion earmarked for FY26 covers highways, railways, semiconductors, and a bullet train that is 80 percent finished. The strategy: spend first, attract private capital after.
news.image_caption: Aerial view of a national highway under construction in India
news.nri_angle: For NRIs considering investments, career moves, or even relocation, India's infrastructure transformation is reshaping the physical reality of the country — faster commutes, better connectivity, and a construction boom that is creating new economic corridors.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Bengaluru's New Gig Workers Wear Cameras on Their Heads. They Are Training Robots to Replace Office Jobs.
news.excerpt: As coding work dries up, India's IT industry is pivoting to 'physical AI' — collecting the movement data that will teach machines to work in the real world. The pay is $3 an hour.
news.image_caption: An industrial robot arm in a laboratory setting, the kind of machine India's IT workers are now training
news.nri_angle: NRI tech professionals who built careers in India's IT outsourcing boom now face a structural shift — the same AI that threatens their coding jobs is creating a new, lower-paid tier of work that their former colleagues are filling.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Caps Diesel Sales at 200 Litres a Day and Bars Bulk Buyers From Petrol Pumps. The Order Lasts 90 Days.
news.excerpt: The most sweeping fuel restrictions since the Iran war began are framed as supply management — not rationing. The government says India has two months of reserves.
news.image_caption: A fuel pump dispensing diesel at a retail outlet
news.nri_angle: NRIs remitting money home face cascading costs as fuel hikes drive inflation, transport costs, and household budgets higher across India.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Zojila Tunnel Just Broke Through. The World's Longest High-Altitude Road Tunnel Is Six Months Ahead of Schedule.
news.excerpt: A controlled blast connected Kashmir and Ladakh through 13 kilometres of Himalayan rock at 11,578 feet. The tunnel will end five months of winter isolation when it opens in 2028.
news.image_caption: A mountain highway in the Ladakh region
news.nri_angle: NRIs planning trips to Ladakh will no longer face the seasonal road-closure window — the tunnel promises year-round access from 2028, transforming winter travel to one of India's most iconic destinations.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Nifty IT Has Lost 27% This Year. The Market Is Not Punishing a Cycle. It Is Repricing an Entire Industry.
news.excerpt: Seven consecutive sessions of losses, 40,000 layoffs, and a TCS chairman who says AI agents will match headcount. The structural reckoning India's outsourcing machine tried to postpone has arrived.
news.image_caption: A modern technology office building in India
news.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs work in IT services or hold IT stocks — the 27% rout directly impacts diaspora wealth and the H-1B pipeline that brought many to the US.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: RBI Just Turned Dollar Deposits Into a 21% Yield Machine for NRIs. The Window Closes September 30.
news.excerpt: Banks are advertising 7 per cent on FCNR deposits. But the real story is what happens when you layer leverage on top. Emkay says a million-dollar deposit could generate $220,000 a year.
news.image_caption: US dollar and Indian rupee currency notes
news.nri_angle: NRIs in the US, UK, Gulf, and Canada with dollar savings now have a narrow window to earn 6-7% (or much more with leverage) in a risk-free-currency deposit at Indian banks — the best FCNR opportunity in years.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: 'These Attacks Must Cease and End.' India Lodges a Second Diplomatic Protest After Three Ships Are Hit in Five Days.
news.excerpt: India's shipping ministry has ordered all agencies on heightened alert. The US has disabled nine vessels and redirected 135 others in its blockade. Three Indian sailors are dead.
news.nri_angle: More than 300,000 Indian sailors serve in global shipping fleets — the Gulf crisis puts their lives at risk while NRIs watch the diplomatic fallout between Delhi and Washington unfold.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Will Be VivaTech's Official AI Partner Country. No Non-European Nation Has Held That Title Before.
news.excerpt: The designation arrives during the India-France Year of Innovation, with India's largest-ever tech delegation heading to Paris next week
news.image_caption: Delegates gather at VivaTech in Paris, where India will serve as the Official AI Partner Country in 2026
news.nri_angle: India's AI Partner Country status creates new career and investment corridors for NRIs in technology between Silicon Valley and Indian tech hubs.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Zepto Just Filed to Raise $837 Million. Its Founders Will Not Sell a Single Share.
news.excerpt: The quick commerce startup's IPO filing reveals a company that doubled revenue to ₹22,624 crore but lost ₹5,905 crore in the process
news.image_caption: Mumbai-based Zepto is preparing to raise 37 million in one of India's most-watched IPOs (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: Zepto's IPO is a test case for NRI investors watching India's consumer tech sector, with Silicon Valley-trained founders betting on a model that has no Western parallel at this scale.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's National Stock Exchange Is About to File Its Own IPO. The Valuation Could Hit ₹6 Trillion.
news.excerpt: After a decade of delays, colocation scandals and regulatory hurdles, the NSE is targeting a June 15 filing that would make it one of India's largest-ever listings
news.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange of India building in Mumbai, home to the world's largest derivatives exchange
news.nri_angle: An NSE listing would give NRI investors direct exposure to India's capital markets infrastructure for the first time, and could reshape how diaspora money flows into Indian equities.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: TCS Will Give 50,000 Employees Access to Anthropic's AI. Its Chairman Wants Equal Numbers of Workers and AI Agents.
news.excerpt: India's largest IT company just struck a global deal with the maker of Claude — the same technology that helped wipe $63 billion off the sector in February
news.image_caption: Tata Consultancy Services headquarters in Mumbai
news.nri_angle: The TCS-Anthropic deal signals a fundamental shift for hundreds of thousands of NRIs working in Indian IT services globally, as the industry pivots from human-led coding to AI agent orchestration.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: BlackRock Says India Has Been 'Over-Punished.' Record Outflows May Have Run Their Course.
news.excerpt: The world's largest asset manager sees India as a top emerging-market conviction — even after $30 billion in foreign money fled and market cap fell behind Taiwan and South Korea
news.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai's Dalal Street
news.nri_angle: NRI investors with India-weighted portfolios face a key question: is the record $30 billion outflow a warning to diversify, or a contrarian signal that BlackRock says the market has already priced in too much bad news?
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Tells Washington: We Do Not Have Overcapacity in Anything. The Section 301 Fight Is Just Beginning.
news.excerpt: India's trade secretary rejects US allegations of structural excess capacity in textiles and steel, days before Modi and Trump are expected to meet at the G7
news.image_caption: India's textile and steel output reflects its domestic demand, not overcapacity, officials say
news.nri_angle: NRIs in pharma, textiles, and IT face direct consequences from the Section 301 outcome — a deal could accelerate India as a post-China manufacturing hub, while tariffs could raise costs and disrupt supply chains.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Gave Its First Space Funding to Private Startups. A Rocket Engine, an AI Satellite Brain, and a Star Tracker Made the Cut.
news.excerpt: IN-SPACe picks three companies under its ₹500 crore Technology Adoption Fund — the first time the Indian government has directly invested in non-governmental space ventures.
news.image_caption: India's Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota, the country's primary launch facility
news.nri_angle: India's private space sector is drawing NRI founders back from NASA and SpaceX, and the government's first direct investment in startups signals the industry has moved beyond aspiration to bankable opportunity.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Twenty-One Years, One Gopuram: Berlin's Sri Ganesha Temple Opens as One of Europe's Largest Hindu Shrines
nri-world.excerpt: Black granite carved in Tamil Nadu, water from the Ganges poured by crane, and a Modi-Merz visit pencilled for October — the Neukölln temple is the diaspora's most ambitious European construction project in a generation.
nri-world.image_caption: The Sri Ganesha Hindu Temple in Berlin's Neukölln district on the day of its consecration, June 7, 2026
nri-world.nri_angle: A two-decade community effort by Berlin's Tamil Hindu diaspora — students, IT workers, Sri Lankan refugees — built one of Europe's largest Hindu temples entirely through donations and volunteer labour, creating a permanent spiritual anchor for South Asians across Germany.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian Banks Are Racing to Offer NRIs Up to 7.1% on Dollar Deposits. The RBI Engineered the Whole Thing.
nri-world.excerpt: A central bank intervention designed to shore up the rupee has turned FCNR deposits into the hottest NRI financial product in a decade, with leverage potentially pushing returns past 20 per cent.
nri-world.image_caption: Indian rupee notes and coins — NRI deposits are now at the centre of a central bank strategy to attract dollars
nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs holding dollars in US or Gulf bank accounts now face a rare window — three-to-five-year FCNR deposits in Indian banks offering returns that rival equities, tax-free in India, with principal fully repatriable. The catch: the scheme closes September 30.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Fifty Years of Chariots on Fifth Avenue: New York's Ratha Yatra Marks a Half-Century of Krishna in America
nri-world.excerpt: What began as a handful of Hare Krishna devotees pulling a homemade chariot through Manhattan in 1976 has become one of the city's longest-running religious processions — and a barometer of how deeply Indian spiritual traditions have rooted in American soil.
nri-world.image_caption: Devotees pull a Ratha Yatra chariot through a street in the United States
nri-world.nri_angle: The NYC Ratha Yatra's 50th anniversary reflects a half-century arc of Indian spiritual culture embedding in America — from counterculture curiosity to mainstream cultural institution, with the festival now drawing as many first-generation Indian professionals and families as it does Western-born devotees.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Three Indian Missions, One Week, Same Warning: Stop Picking Up the Phone
nri-world.excerpt: Consulates in Toronto, New York, and the Bay Area are all sounding the alarm on a coordinated wave of phone scams targeting NRIs — and the timing tells you why.
nri-world.image_caption: A smartphone displaying a fraud alert notification
nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs across North America are being targeted by sophisticated phone scams impersonating Indian consular officials, exploiting immigration anxieties in the current political climate.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Fifteen Languages, Three Days, One Theatre: NYIFF 2026 Is the Most Important Indian Film Festival You Have Never Heard Of
nri-world.excerpt: The New York Indian Film Festival returns for its 26th edition next week with Nawazuddin Siddiqui, a Dil Chahta Hai anniversary screening, and films in languages spoken by fewer than two million people.
nri-world.image_caption: Nawazuddin Siddiqui at an Indian film festival
nri-world.nri_angle: NYIFF is a cultural lifeline for Indian Americans seeking cinema that reflects the diversity of their homeland — far beyond the Bollywood mainstream — and a launchpad for filmmakers from India's margins.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: From Hyderabad's JNTU to Alabama's Rocket City: Srinath Ekkad Named Engineering Dean at UAH
nri-world.excerpt: A thermal sciences researcher who started at Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University will now lead one of America's most aerospace-connected engineering colleges.
nri-world.image_caption: The Engineering Building at the University of Alabama in Huntsville
nri-world.nri_angle: Ekkad's appointment extends a pattern of Indian-origin academics reaching the highest rungs of American university leadership, from JNTU undergrad to dean of UAH's 3,000-student engineering college.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India's Sports Ministry Has Sent a 'Sports Passport' Proposal to the PM's Office. For Diaspora Athletes, It Changes Everything.
nri-world.excerpt: If approved, the framework could let PIO and OCI athletes represent India in international competition without surrendering foreign citizenship — a first in Indian sports history, and a potential game-changer ahead of the 2036 Olympics bid.
nri-world.image_caption: India's national football team in action during the 2018 SAFF Championship
nri-world.nri_angle: Millions of Indian-origin athletes who grew up playing football, tennis, and basketball in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia have been legally barred from representing India. The Sports Passport proposal directly addresses the diaspora's exclusion from Indian national teams.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Three Decades at MIT Press, and Now She Runs Columbia's. Meet Gita Manaktala.
nri-world.excerpt: Columbia University has appointed the Indian American publishing leader as Executive Director of one of the nation's oldest and most respected university presses — a quiet milestone in a field where South Asian representation at the top remains rare.
nri-world.image_caption: Columbia University's Morningside Heights campus in New York City
nri-world.nri_angle: Manaktala's appointment adds to the growing but still thin ranks of Indian Americans leading major American academic and cultural institutions — a quieter form of diaspora achievement than tech CEO headlines, but one that shapes what knowledge gets published, who gets heard, and which ideas reach global audiences.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Three Bay Area Hindu Temples Hit in Weeks. All Five Indian-American Lawmakers Just Demanded Answers.
nri-world.excerpt: In an unprecedented move, every Indian-American member of Congress has written jointly to the DOJ after a wave of pro-Khalistan vandalism struck temples from Hayward to Newark. The State Department and India's foreign minister have also weighed in.
nri-world.image_caption: A Hindu temple in California, representative of the community institutions being targeted
nri-world.nri_angle: Hindu temples in the Bay Area — the heart of the Indian-American tech community — are being systematically targeted, prompting an unprecedented joint response from all five Indian-American members of Congress.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Fifty-Six Years After a Prayer at Le Bourget, France Is Getting Its First Traditional Hindu Temple
nri-world.excerpt: The BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Bussy-Saint-Georges opens in September with a thirteen-day Festival of Culture — a milestone for Europe's Indian diaspora that began with a 1970 airport layover.
nri-world.image_caption: Carved stone deities at a traditional Hindu temple — the same craft tradition behind the Paris mandir
nri-world.nri_angle: The Paris mandir fills a gap for hundreds of thousands of Indians across Western Europe who have lacked a traditionally built stone temple, and its September inauguration is already drawing NRI families from the US, UK, and Gulf into pilgrimage-tourism packages.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Singapore Just Blocked Fourteen Posts Targeting Its Indian Community. The Content Likely Came from China.
nri-world.excerpt: The city-state invoked its Online Criminal Harms Act to order YouTube, Facebook, and X to disable videos claiming Singapore was being 'overrun by Indians' — a rare, swift use of state power to defend diaspora communities.
nri-world.image_caption: A street in Little India, Singapore, adorned with colourful cultural decorations
nri-world.nri_angle: Singapore's decisive legal intervention to protect its Indian minority offers a sharp contrast to how other countries with large NRI populations have responded to anti-Indian sentiment — and raises questions about what legal tools are available elsewhere.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Seven 'Ratnas' and a 57-Year Legacy: Inside the AIA-NY Annual Benefit Gala 2026
nri-world.excerpt: The oldest Indian-American organisation honoured a xenotransplantation pioneer, a Harvard AI entrepreneur, and five other trailblazers at a packed Flushing gathering — then announced plans for its 39th Deepavali celebration.
nri-world.image_caption: The Association of Indians in America held its annual gala at Terrace on the Park in Flushing, New York
nri-world.nri_angle: Oldest Indian-American organisation (founded 1967) honours new generation of NRI achievers; event bridges generational and professional divides in the community.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Just Threw Open Its Bond Market to the World. For NRI Investors, the Timing Could Not Be Better.
markets-finance.excerpt: Tax exemptions, subsidised hedging, and a $3 billion corporate debt rush — India's most aggressive capital-market reforms in years are rewriting the playbook for overseas fixed-income investors, with Bloomberg index inclusion now weeks away from a decision.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building, headquarters of the central bank driving India's bond-market reforms
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI depositors benefit directly from RBI's fully subsidised hedging on foreign currency deposits, while the tax exemptions on government bonds make Indian fixed income a viable portfolio allocation for the first time in years — particularly for diaspora investors burned by the rupee's depreciation and looking for yield with policy support.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: El Nino Is Officially Here. India's Monsoon, Food Prices, and NRI Portfolios Are All in the Firing Line.
markets-finance.excerpt: The US Climate Prediction Center and India's Met department have both confirmed moderate-to-strong El Nino conditions during the monsoon season — the first since 2023 and potentially one of the strongest on record. Here is what it means for your money.
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors with Indian equity, bond, or commodity exposure face direct portfolio risk from El Nino through FMCG margin compression, rupee weakness, and potential RBI policy shifts.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: BlackRock and Lighthouse Canton Say India Has Been 'Over-Punished.' The Contrarian Case for NRI Investors Is Getting Louder.
markets-finance.excerpt: After a record 30 billion dollars in foreign outflows, the world's largest asset manager and a major wealth firm argue that India's lack of a direct AI play is an advantage — not a liability — and that the worst of the selloff may be over.
markets-finance.image_caption: A stock market trading screen displaying financial data and price movements
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors who paused SIPs or sold India positions during the record $30 billion outflow are now hearing from BlackRock and Lighthouse Canton that the selloff has gone too far — a signal that could reshape diaspora portfolio decisions.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Vedanta Splits Into Five: Four Demerged Companies Hit the Stock Market on Monday. Here Is What NRI Investors Need to Know.
markets-finance.excerpt: The largest corporate demerger in Indian history reaches its final act as Vedanta Aluminium, Vedanta Oil & Gas, Vedanta Power, and Vedanta Iron & Steel begin trading on the BSE and NSE on June 15 — creating pure-play bets on India's commodity future.
markets-finance.image_caption: Anil Agarwal, founder and chairman of Vedanta Resources, whose demerger creates four new listed companies on Monday (Wikimedia Commons)
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs holding Vedanta shares through demat or overseas broker accounts will find four new stocks in their portfolios on Monday — understanding the listing mechanics, trade restrictions, and tax implications is essential before the first trade.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: US-Iran Peace Deal Hopes Send Nifty Soaring 2%: What the Oil Shock Reversal Means for Indian Markets and NRI Portfolios
markets-finance.excerpt: A surprise memorandum of understanding between Washington and Tehran triggered the biggest single-day rally in months, with crude prices tumbling and Indian equities surging across sectors
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street, Mumbai — Indian equities surged on US-Iran peace deal hopes
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investment portfolios, oil price impact on Indian economy, forex and remittance implications
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Gold Tariff Gamble: A 15% Import Duty, a $14 Billion Smuggling Surge, and the NRI Caught in Between
markets-finance.excerpt: New Delhi's bid to curb gold demand and protect forex reserves has revived grey-market channels that could move over 100 tonnes this year.
markets-finance.image_caption: Gold remains culturally central to Indian weddings and festivals, making tariff hikes a deeply personal issue for the diaspora.
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs who regularly send gold home for weddings and festivals, the tariff hike means higher costs, more scrutiny at customs, and a growing temptation to use grey-market channels — with serious legal consequences.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Nifty Surges Nearly 2% on Iran Peace Hopes as RBI Opens a Dollar Goldmine for NRI Depositors
markets-finance.excerpt: Indian markets posted their best single-day gain in two months as oil prices collapsed on US-Iran deal optimism — and the RBI's subsidised hedging programme is making NRI dollar deposits the most attractive they have been in years
markets-finance.image_caption: A stock market display showing real-time financial data — the Nifty 50 posted its best day in two months on Iran peace hopes
markets-finance.nri_angle: Banks are offering NRIs 6-7% on dollar FCNR deposits with RBI-subsidised hedging — a rare window that closes in September; diaspora investors should evaluate before the deadline.

markets-finance.title: India Opens Insurance to 100% Foreign Ownership — What NRIs Need to Know
markets-finance.excerpt: The landmark reform allows global insurers to fully own Indian companies, promising better products for the diaspora and reshaping a $143 billion market
markets-finance.image_caption: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman — India has opened its insurance sector to 100% foreign ownership (Wikimedia Commons)
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs stand to gain from cross-border insurance products, easier policy servicing, and new investment opportunities as global insurers enter India with full ownership.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Braces for a Wider Fiscal Deficit as Iran War Costs Mount and the Fed Signals No Relief
markets-finance.excerpt: New Delhi may let the deficit hit 4.8% of GDP to absorb energy subsidies, even as US inflation surges to 4.2% and the rupee tests new lows — but a potential Iran deal could change everything.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian currency notes — the rupee has fallen to 95.68 against the dollar as foreign investors pull record capital from Indian markets.
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs sending remittances are benefiting from a weaker rupee, but those with Indian investments face a double hit from falling equity markets and currency depreciation — making asset allocation decisions more urgent than ever.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's $315-Billion IT Empire Faces Its AI Reckoning
markets-finance.excerpt: TCS chairman says AI agents will match headcount. Nifty IT is down 25%. And the outsourcing model that built India's middle class is being rewritten in real time
markets-finance.image_caption: Tata Consultancy Services, India's largest IT company, where chairman N. Chandrasekaran announced AI agents will soon match the firm's 600,000 employees
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors hold significant positions in Indian IT stocks; the sector's 25% decline represents billions in diaspora wealth erosion. The structural shift affects the economic trajectory of young Indians who viewed software engineering as their path to prosperity.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Just Abolished All Taxes on Foreign Bond Investment. One Billion Dollars Flowed In Within Three Days.
markets-finance.excerpt: The tax exemption and expanded market access are designed to lure back foreign capital and lock in a spot in the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index. Here is what it means for NRI investors.

markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors stand to benefit directly from expanded access to Indian government bonds and the removal of tax barriers — the reforms also strengthen the case for FCNR deposits and may stabilise the rupee that has hit their remittance calculations hard this year.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Corporate Borrowers Are Racing to Lock In Lower Rates. The RBI's Dollar Blitz Just Opened a Window.
markets-finance.excerpt: Companies have launched more than $3 billion in bond sales this week after the central bank's forex measures slashed borrowing costs by 40 basis points. For NRI fixed-income investors, the calculus is shifting.

sports.title: He Went Unsold at INR 1.5 Crore. On Saturday, He Hit Eight Sixes Against India.
sports.excerpt: Rahmanullah Gurbaz smashed the fastest century by an Afghan batter in ODIs — 102 off 51 balls in a rain-shortened 25-over match in Dharamsala. Not a single IPL franchise wanted him six months ago.
sports.image_caption: The HPCA Stadium in Dharamsala, where Gurbaz scored his record-breaking 102 off 51 balls
sports.nri_angle: Afghan batter went unsold in IPL 2026 — diaspora fans in US, UK, Canada watching him dismantle India's bowling shows the gap between franchise valuations and international talent.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: He Was Bowling in the Nets in 2019. On Saturday, He Took Three Wickets on Debut.
sports.excerpt: Gurnoor Brar, a 6-foot-5 right-arm seamer from Muktsar in Punjab, struck in his very first over for India and finished with 3/27 in a rain-shortened ODI against Afghanistan at Dharamsala.
sports.image_caption: HPCA Stadium in Dharamsala, where Gurnoor Brar made his ODI debut for India against Afghanistan
sports.nri_angle: Punjab-origin fast bowler rises from domestic cricket and IPL net bowling to earning an India cap — a story of the Ranji Trophy pipeline that resonates with NRIs from Punjab watching from abroad.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Burned Cars, Anti-Immigrant Riots, and India's T20I Tour of Belfast Hanging by a Thread
sports.excerpt: The BCCI is monitoring escalating violence in Northern Ireland as Cricket Ireland weighs whether to relocate the June 26-28 matches. For the Indian community in Belfast, the stakes go beyond cricket.
sports.image_caption: Shreyas Iyer, named captain for India T20I tour of Ireland
sports.nri_angle: Indian community in Belfast faces uncertainty as anti-immigrant violence threatens the first India cricket tour to Northern Ireland since 2007.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Russia Suspended From World Chess. India’s Gukesh and Vaishali Are Waiting on the Other Side.

lifestyle-health.title: Four Minutes of Exercise a Day Quadrupled Fitness in Adults Over 65. For the Diaspora, This Changes Everything About Aging Parents.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Penn State study found that push-ups, chair stands, rows and stair steps — just 30 seconds each — produced dramatic strength gains in 12 weeks. The implications for NRI families managing elder care across oceans are profound.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A senior man performing push-ups at home as part of a daily fitness routine
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For millions of NRI families managing aging parents' health from thousands of miles away, a research-backed four-minute daily routine that requires no gym and no equipment beyond resistance bands could be the most practical intervention they can actually implement remotely.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Men and Women Need Different Diets to Live Longer. A 104,000-Person Study Just Proved It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Coffee extends male lifespan by up to three years. Fish does the same for women. Both sexes benefit from cutting processed food — but the optimal longevity diet is not one-size-fits-all, and the South Asian kitchen may already hold the advantage.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Grilled fish with fresh vegetables and spices — the Mediterranean staples linked to female longevity
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: The study's findings align strikingly well with traditional Indian dietary patterns — high legume and vegetable intake, extensive use of spices and turmeric, fish-heavy coastal cuisines, and daily coffee or tea rituals — suggesting that diaspora families preserving these food traditions may already be on the right track.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Daily Pill Just Doubled Pancreatic Cancer Survival. The Audience at ASCO Gave It a Standing Ovation.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Daraxonrasib is the first drug ever to meaningfully extend life in metastatic pancreatic cancer — a disease that kills 95 per cent of patients within five years. For South Asians, whose pancreatic cancer rates are climbing, the breakthrough could not be more urgent.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A researcher examines pharmaceutical compounds in a laboratory setting
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Pancreatic cancer incidence is rising among South Asians in India and abroad; daraxonrasib's oral delivery and universal mechanism offer hope regardless of geography or healthcare access.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Ninety Minutes of Weights Per Week Cut Dementia Deaths by 27 Per Cent. South Asians Cannot Afford to Ignore This.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A 30-year Harvard study of 147,000 adults found that moderate resistance training slashed death from neurological disease, heart disease, and all causes — with a ceiling effect that makes the prescription achievable for anyone.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A man lifts heavy dumbbells during a strength training session at a gym
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians have among the lowest exercise rates globally and face elevated cardiovascular and dementia risk; this study offers a specific, achievable prescription.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Single Brain Injection Restored Dopamine in 87% of Parkinson's Patients. The Gene Therapy Era May Have Arrived.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Phase 1 trial of BBM-P002, a dual-target gene therapy, showed sustained motor improvement after 12 months with no serious side effects — offering hope to the estimated one million Indians living with Parkinson's and to diaspora families watching from abroad.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A digital rendering of the human brain, illustrating the neural pathways targeted by gene therapy
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Parkinson's disease affects an estimated one million Indians and is rising sharply in the diaspora; gene therapy breakthroughs will reach high-income countries first, leaving NRI families navigating a two-tier access system.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Heart Scan That Saved Millions of Lives Just Got Its First AI Upgrade. For South Asians, It Could Not Have Come Sooner.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Agatston-2.0, published in the American Journal of Preventive Cardiology, uses artificial intelligence to detect hidden coronary calcium in patients whose conventional scans showed a clean zero — a finding that matters disproportionately for a community with two to four times the average cardiovascular risk.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A CT scanner used for cardiac imaging in a modern hospital facility
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians suffer heart attacks at younger ages and higher rates than almost any other ethnic group; an AI upgrade that catches early coronary calcium missed by conventional scans could save thousands of diaspora lives.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Joint Pain Pill Millions Take May Be Accelerating Alzheimer's. A 60,000-Patient Study Just Flagged It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Glucosamine, one of the world's most popular over-the-counter supplements, is linked to a 25 per cent faster progression from mild cognitive impairment to dementia — and the mechanism may involve sugar molecules hijacking brain proteins.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Supplement capsules spilling from a white bottle
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Glucosamine is widely used among South Asian families for joint and knee pain, making this finding directly relevant to older NRIs and their parents back home.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Americans Born After 1970 Are Dying Faster Than Their Parents Did. The Data Is Alarming.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Tufts University study tracking 45 years of mortality data reveals that Gen Xers and elder millennials face rising death rates from heart disease, cancer, and drug overdoses — reversing a century of progress that many immigrant families took for granted.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A doctor examines a middle-aged patient during a routine health check
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Many NRIs moved to America expecting better health outcomes for their families, but this data shows the country they adopted is quietly failing an entire generation — including their own children growing up here.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Gut Bacteria Could Fight Cancer: The Probiotic Trial That's Rewriting Oncology

lifestyle-health.title: Harvard Study Links Ultraprocessed Foods to 58% Higher Dementia Risk — A Wake-Up Call for the Diaspora Diet

lifestyle-health.title: Low Vitamin C Levels Linked to Smaller, Less Connected Brains in New Study — And South Asian Diets May Offer an Edge

lifestyle-health.image_caption: Higher vitamin C levels in the blood were associated with greater grey matter volume and stronger brain connectivity in adults over 64.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Traditional South Asian diets are naturally rich in vitamin C through amla (Indian gooseberry), citrus fruits, guava, and fresh chutneys — a dietary advantage that may help protect brain health as the diaspora ages.

food.excerpt: Grown in the Indus Valley five millennia ago and revered by Ayurvedic healers, the ancient seed is now showing up in Starbucks drinks, protein bowls, and a $17.5 billion global market.
food.image_caption: Black sesame seeds, an ancient superfood now driving one of 2026's biggest food trends

food.title: 12,653 and Counting: Inside the Unstoppable Rise of Indian Restaurants Across America
food.excerpt: From classic New Jersey diners turning into biryani joints to vegan dosa houses in Phoenix, Indian cuisine is reshaping America's dining landscape at a pace not seen before.
food.image_caption: Indian cuisine has become one of America's fastest-growing dining categories, with over 12,600 restaurants nationwide (Wikimedia Commons)

carousel.title: America's Top Trade Negotiator Will Fly to India the Week After G7. A Deal, Officials Say, Is Possible.
carousel.excerpt: USTR Jamieson Greer's visit follows months of back-and-forth on tariffs, Section 301 probes, and a bilateral framework that could reshape how NRIs send goods — and money — across both countries.
carousel.image_caption: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer at his official portrait session
carousel.nri_angle: A US-India trade deal directly affects NRI remittances, tariffs on Indian exports, H-1B visa policy, and the cost of goods flowing between the two countries.

carousel.title: Hrithik Roshan Just Signed with the Company Behind Spotlight and The Revenant. He's Done Waiting for Bollywood to Let Him Grow Up.
carousel.excerpt: Anonymous Content — the Hollywood powerhouse that built careers around prestige cinema — will now represent India's biggest action star internationally. The deal arrives as he directs Krrish 4, produces for Prime Video, and quietly admits he's tired of playing the hero.
carousel.image_caption: Hrithik Roshan at a public appearance (Wikimedia Commons)

carousel.title: He Went Unsold at INR 1.5 Crore. On Saturday, He Hit Eight Sixes Against India.
carousel.excerpt: Rahmanullah Gurbaz smashed the fastest century by an Afghan batter in ODIs — 102 off 51 balls in a rain-shortened 25-over match in Dharamsala. Not a single IPL franchise wanted him six months ago.
carousel.image_caption: The HPCA Stadium in Dharamsala, where Gurbaz scored his record-breaking 102 off 51 balls
carousel.nri_angle: Afghan batter went unsold in IPL 2026 — diaspora fans in US, UK, Canada watching him dismantle India's bowling shows the gap between franchise valuations and international talent.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: KPMG Pulled Its Own AI Report After It Turned Out to Be Full of Fabrications
carousel.excerpt: Only five of 45 citations were accurate. UBS, the NHS, and Swiss railways all denied the claims made about them. Welcome to 'vibe citing.'
carousel.image_caption: KPMG has withdrawn its agentic AI report pending investigation
carousel.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of Indians work at Big Four firms and IT consultancies now deploying AI in client work — this scandal is a warning about what happens when oversight fails.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk

carousel.title: India Just Threw Open Its Bond Market to the World. For NRI Investors, the Timing Could Not Be Better.
carousel.excerpt: Tax exemptions, subsidised hedging, and a $3 billion corporate debt rush — India's most aggressive capital-market reforms in years are rewriting the playbook for overseas fixed-income investors, with Bloomberg index inclusion now weeks away from a decision.
carousel.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building, headquarters of the central bank driving India's bond-market reforms
carousel.nri_angle: NRI depositors benefit directly from RBI's fully subsidised hedging on foreign currency deposits, while the tax exemptions on government bonds make Indian fixed income a viable portfolio allocation for the first time in years — particularly for diaspora investors burned by the rupee's depreciation and looking for yield with policy support.
carousel.author: Diaspora Desk
